title: a copy length was clamped to the buffer size, so the terminator landed one past it
object: the caller-supplied output buffer of buf_len bytes, one direct allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a copy clamped to the capacity rather than to the capacity minus the terminator
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: `address_to_str_buf` no longer exists in v4.6.8:epan/to_str.c (`grep -c address_to_str_buf` = 0), so the construct was REMOVED rather than fixed and the pinned code cannot carry the defect. A fix-reversal against history.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm's access crosses the allocation and the case's damage flag is set; the fixed arm's bound keeps it inside. The arms differ by the upstream fix, not by protection. status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- wiretap, wsutil and ui do not use wmem, and epan/uat.c and epan/charsets.c take the crossed buffer from g_malloc or from the caller -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the copy itself never crosses -- it is clamped correctly to `buf_len` -- and the crossing is the TERMINATOR written after it, at `buf[copy_len]`. So a check that only validated the memmove would pass, and the fix changes the clamp rather than the store.
